key_list_texts.name: genuine
key_list_texts.description: The signed list as written: every member is covered by the signature.

key_list_texts.name: defaults_left_out
key_list_texts.description: B's revoked and archived_versions are left out. The signature covers them at their defaults, false and empty, so nothing is outside it.

key_list_texts.name: members_outside_the_signature
key_list_texts.description: B's record gains superseded_by_hex and retired_at, and D's a public_key_hex holding B's key. The signature does not cover them, so they would show B's key retired.

key_list_texts.name: member_name_escaped_in_the_pointer
key_list_texts.description: B's record gains a member named retired/at~. The pointer writes / as ~1 and ~ as ~0.

key_list_texts.name: archived_at_written_null
key_list_texts.description: B's active record gains archived_at written as null. The signature covers the record without it, so the member written is not covered.

key_list_texts.name: marker_written_false
key_list_texts.description: The hosted authority's marker is written as false. The signature covers the list without a false marker, so the member written is not covered.

key_list_texts.name: member_name_written_with_an_escape
key_list_texts.description: B's revoked is written with its first letter as the escape \u0072. A parser reads the same name, so the signature covers it and nothing is outside it.

key_list_texts.name: authority_written_twice
key_list_texts.description: A second copy of B, holding B's key archived in hex, is written before the real one. A parser keeps the last copy, so the signature verifies and no check reads the first.

key_list_texts.name: pqc_signature_written_null
key_list_texts.description: The reserved pqc_manifest_signature is written as null. No signature covers either signature member, so their values are not compared and nothing is outside it.

head_texts.name: genuine
head_texts.description: The good chain's heads as written: no member is written twice.

head_texts.name: issued_at_written_twice
head_texts.description: Head 1 writes issued_at twice, the earlier copy dated an hour later. The checks would read the last copy, which the signature covers.

head_texts.name: head_written_twice
head_texts.description: Head 2 writes its head twice, the earlier copy under authority B.

head_texts.name: signature_written_twice
head_texts.description: Head 3 writes its signature twice, the earlier copy head 1's signature.

head_texts.name: key_version_written_twice
head_texts.description: Head 1 writes signing_key_version twice, the earlier copy 8.

head_texts.name: signature_written_twice_once_escaped
head_texts.description: Head 2 writes its signature twice, the earlier copy's name with the escape \u0073. A parser reads the same name, so it is one member written twice.

cases.name: good_chain
cases.description: Three proofs, three heads under the proofs' authority: (a), (b), (c), (f) ok; (d), (e) need a transparency log, so the population carries the label.

cases.name: withheld_proof
cases.description: Head 2 names a proof that was not handed: (c) fails; (f) cannot compare head 2 with its proof.

f_head_signatures.reason: a named proof was not handed

cases.name: withheld_head
cases.description: Head 3 of four was withheld: head 4 links to a head that was not handed (a) and the sequence skips 3 (b); proof 3 is listed as unwitnessed.

cases.name: head_links_past_the_head_below_it
cases.description: Head 3 carries the hash of head 1, a lower handed head but not the one at the greatest lower sequence: (a) fails.

cases.name: sequence_gap
cases.description: The signer linked its third head correctly but numbered it 4: (b) fails, (a) holds.

cases.name: heads_handed_out_of_order
cases.description: The same three heads handed as 3, 1, 2. A verifier reads them by sequence: nothing fails.

cases.name: chain_without_head_1
cases.description: Heads 2 and 3 alone: they link to each other, so (a) holds, and a chain starts at sequence 1, so (b) fails. Proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: fork
cases.description: Two heads at sequence 2, both linked to head 1, naming different proofs: (b) fails.

cases.name: wrong_authority
cases.description: Heads signed by another registered authority (B) over authority A's proofs: (f) fails at the proofs' authority, before any signature is read, so it would fail whoever signed.

cases.name: non_canonical_signature
cases.description: Head 2's genuine signature with S replaced by S + L: (f) fails. Plain verification refuses this as well, so small_order_key is the case that proves strictness.

cases.name: small_order_key
cases.description: Head 2 names key version 2, registered as the identity point, with R = identity and S = 0. A non-strict verifier accepts that signature for any message; strict verification refuses the small-order key, so (f) fails.

cases.name: forged_authority_claim
cases.description: Head 2 claims authority A's key but was signed with authority B's: (f) fails.

cases.name: relabelled_authority
cases.description: A head authority A signed, with its authority_id changed to B, naming B's own proof. The authority is inside the signed bytes, so the signature covers another head and (f) fails.

cases.name: authority_switch_mid_chain
cases.description: Head 1 is under authority A; head 2, correctly linked, is under authority B and names B's own proof. Every signature verifies, and (f) fails because a chain belongs to one authority.

cases.name: two_authorities_at_sequence_one
cases.description: Two heads at sequence 1 under two authorities. The result names the first handed, and (b) and (f) both fail.

cases.name: local_signer_and_hosted_proofs_carry_the_label
cases.description: A local-signer proof and proofs under two authorities the key list does not mark as emitting heads, with no heads: nothing fails, all three are listed as unwitnessed, and the population carries the label.

cases.name: head_names_local_signer_proof
cases.description: A customer head names a local-signer proof, which emits no heads: (f) fails.

cases.name: head_names_hosted_proof
cases.description: A customer head names a hosted proof, which emits no heads: (f) fails.

cases.name: head_under_hosted_authority_names_customer_proof
cases.description: A head under a hosted authority names a customer's proof. The proof is listed and anchored, so (c) holds; the head's authority emits no heads, so (f) fails before any key is read.

cases.name: head_under_unmarked_authority
cases.description: A head under an authority the key list carries without the marker, naming that authority's own proof: it emits no heads, so (f) fails.

cases.name: head_under_authority_not_in_the_key_list
cases.description: A head under an authority the key list does not carry: it is not known to emit no heads, and it has no registered key, so (f) fails.

cases.name: proof_under_authority_not_in_the_key_list
cases.description: A proof under an authority the key list does not carry, with no head: listed as having no handed head.

cases.name: no_key_list_knows_only_the_local_signer
cases.description: No key list, so only the local signer is known to emit no heads: the hosted proof is listed as having no handed head.

cases.name: no_key_list
cases.description: The good chain with no key list: (f) cannot resolve head keys and is not checked; nothing fails.

cases.name: proof_without_a_head
cases.description: Two heads and a third proof of the same authority with no head: listed as unwitnessed, not a failure. A cut tail is found only by (e).

cases.name: first_head_without_genesis_link
cases.description: The head at sequence 1 does not carry the genesis link: (a) fails.

cases.name: tip_named_twice
cases.description: Heads 1 and 2 both name proof 1: (c) fails.

cases.name: forged_copy_before_genuine
cases.description: A copy of proof 2 with destruction_state edited, handed before the genuine proof 2. It keeps the leaf, because the leaf does not cover the canonical view, but its signature no longer verifies. Every handed proof with the named leaf must verify, so (c) and (f) both fail on the forged copy whatever the order.

cases.name: forged_copy_after_genuine
cases.description: A copy of proof 2 with destruction_state edited, handed after the genuine proof 2. It keeps the leaf, because the leaf does not cover the canonical view, but its signature no longer verifies. Every handed proof with the named leaf must verify, so (c) and (f) both fail on the forged copy whatever the order.

cases.name: one_proof_named_twice_through_an_unsigned_field
cases.description: Proof 1 and a copy with attestation.key_id rewritten. The key_id is in the leaf but not under the signature, so the leaves differ and both copies verify. Head 1 names proof 1 and head 2 names the copy; both signatures cover one message under one authority, so (c) fails: one document is named twice.

cases.name: head_key_under_two_authorities
cases.description: Authority D's key is also listed under authority E. A head signed with it cannot be tied to one authority, so (f) fails.

cases.name: copy_without_public_key_has_no_leaf
cases.description: The head names proof 1's leaf, but the only copy handed carries its key under verification_key instead of public_key. The leaf reads public_key only, so the copy has no leaf: (c) fails, and the copy is listed as unwitnessed with no tip.

f_head_signatures.reason: a named proof was not handed

cases.name: head_key_archived_under_a_revoked_authority
cases.description: Authority F's key is also among the archived versions of authority G, which the key list marks revoked. A revoked authority and an archived version still list the key, so a head signed with it cannot be tied to one authority, and (f) fails.

cases.name: head_key_listed_again_with_a_base64_prefix
cases.description: Authority I lists authority H's key with a base64: prefix. Keys are compared as decoded bytes, so the prefixed listing is the same key, and (f) fails.

cases.name: genesis_misplaced
cases.description: Head 2 carries the genesis link, which only the head at sequence 1 may carry: (a) fails.

cases.name: named_proof_not_verified
cases.description: Head 2 names a proof whose only handed copy has destruction_state edited: its signature does not verify, so (c) fails, and it is not anchored, so (f) fails.

cases.name: head_signing_key_unknown
cases.description: Head 2 names key version 9 of authority A, which the key list does not hold: (f) fails.

cases.name: head_authority_revoked
cases.description: Heads under an authority the key list marks revoked, naming that authority's own proof: (f) fails.

cases.name: head_algorithm_unsupported
cases.description: Head 2 names key version 3 of authority A, which the key list records as an ML-DSA-65 key; this verifier checks head signatures only as Ed25519, so (f) fails.

cases.name: named_proof_not_anchored
cases.description: Head 2 names a proof that claims authority A's key version 1 but was signed with a key no authority lists. It verifies under its embedded key, so (c) holds; it does not verify under the key list, so (f) fails.

cases.name: identical_head_handed_twice
cases.description: Head 2 is handed twice, the same bytes under the same key version. A copy is not a fork, so (a), (b) and (c) read it once, and each copy's signature verifies.

cases.name: identical_copy_with_a_bad_signature
cases.description: Head 2 is handed twice under the same key version, the second copy signed with another key. (a), (b) and (c) read one head, and (f) checks every copy, so (f) fails.

cases.name: same_head_under_two_key_versions
cases.description: One head body signed under key versions 1 and 8, both in window. The signer used two keys at one sequence, so they stay two heads: (b) and (c) fail, and (f) holds.

cases.name: named_proof_has_no_signature
cases.description: The named proof has an empty signature. It is valid as far as stage 4, and that is short of both bars: (c) needs stage 7 and (f) needs stage 8.

cases.name: chain_continues_across_key_rotation
cases.description: Head 1 is under key version 8, issued before that version was archived; head 2 is under version 1. Nothing fails. Registration does not produce this shape today: the registration design gates marking on the rotation model.

cases.name: head_after_its_key_was_archived
cases.description: Head 2 is issued after key version 8 was archived. The head is not shown to be inside the key's window, so (f) fails.

cases.name: head_before_its_key_took_effect
cases.description: Head 2 is issued before key version 4 took effect. The head is not shown to be inside the key's window, so (f) fails.

cases.name: key_list_effective_from_unreadable
cases.description: Key version 5's effective_from cannot be read. The head is not shown to be inside the key's window, so (f) fails.

cases.name: key_list_archived_at_unreadable
cases.description: Key version 6's archived_at cannot be read. The head is not shown to be inside the key's window, so (f) fails.

cases.name: archived_key_with_no_end
cases.description: Key version 7 is archived with no archived_at. The head is not shown to be inside the key's window, so (f) fails.

cases.name: head_issued_before_the_head_below_it
cases.description: Head 2 was issued a second before head 1: (b) fails, because a chain runs forward in time.

cases.name: heads_share_a_second
cases.description: Two heads in one second: time stands still between them, it does not go back.

cases.name: retired_key_backdates_a_head
cases.description: Key version 8 was archived, and it extends the chain with a head dated inside its window. Its signature and window hold; (b) fails, because the head is older than the head below it.

cases.name: v1_0_proof_named
cases.description: A cdp_version 1.0 signature covers final_hash alone, so the proof does not show which authority it is under: (f) fails, whatever authority it names.

cases.name: v1_0_proof_named_no_key_list
cases.description: The same head with no key list: (f) needs no key list to refuse it.

cases.name: v2_2_proof_named
cases.description: A cdp_version 2.2 signature covers the proof's authority, so a head may name it.

cases.name: proof_under_a_shared_key_named_by_the_other_authority
cases.description: Authority E lists authority D's key. A proof signed under E is not D's, and a head under D that names it fails (f), though the key is D's too.

cases.name: proof_authority_writes_a_line
cases.description: A proof's authority holds a newline, a forged check line and a terminal erase sequence. Whoever holds the key can sign that: (f) fails. The population CLI tests prove a reader's output escapes it.

cases.name: unwitnessed_attestation_pointer_claims_local
cases.description: The proof verifies, and a copy of the key version inside the attestation says the local signer, but the key list holds its key. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: unwitnessed_attestation_pointer_claims_local_unlisted_key
cases.description: The proof names the local signer's authority under a key the list does not hold, with a numeric key version. A copy of the key version inside the attestation says the local signer. No signature covers that copy, so it is not read. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: unwitnessed_authority_set_to_local
cases.description: The proof's authority was changed to the local signer's name, so its signature no longer verifies and nothing it says about its signer can be read. The reason is proof_not_verified.

cases.name: unwitnessed_authority_set_to_hosted
cases.description: The proof's authority was changed to a hosted one, so its signature no longer verifies and nothing it says about its signer can be read. The reason is proof_not_verified.

cases.name: unwitnessed_authority_deleted
cases.description: The proof's authority was deleted, which reads as the hosted default; its signature no longer verifies. The reason is proof_not_verified.

cases.name: unwitnessed_empty_document
cases.description: An empty document is not a proof of any signer. The reason is proof_not_verified.

cases.name: unwitnessed_authority_only_document
cases.description: A document holding only a hosted authority is not a hosted proof. The reason is proof_not_verified.

cases.name: unwitnessed_version_0_relabelled_local
cases.description: A key version 0 proof relabelled local verifies, but the key list holds its key under version 8, so it is not the local signer's. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: unwitnessed_version_0_relabelled_local_no_key_list
cases.description: The same proof with no key list: its signature covers authority A, so it does not name the local signer. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: unwitnessed_version_0_relabelled_local_unlisted_authority
cases.description: A key version 0 proof under an authority the list does not carry, relabelled local. The list does not hold its key, but its signature covers that authority, so it does not name the local signer. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: unwitnessed_throwaway_key_keeps_a_marked_authority
cases.description: A proof signed with a key anyone can mint, carrying the local signer's key version and keeping an authority that emits heads. Its signature covers that authority, so it does not name the local signer. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: unwitnessed_local_version_on_a_hosted_authority
cases.description: The local signer's key version under a hosted authority's name, which the local signer no longer writes. Its signature covers the hosted name. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: unwitnessed_local_name_under_a_listed_key
cases.description: The signature covers the local signer's name and the proof carries its key version, but the key list holds the key, so a key holder wrote those words. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: unwitnessed_local_name_on_version_1_0
cases.description: A version 1.0 proof names the local signer in fields its signature does not cover. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: unwitnessed_hosted_name_on_an_unlisted_key
cases.description: The proof names a hosted authority and verifies alone, but not under that authority's listed key, so it is not shown to be hosted. The reason is no_handed_head.

cases.name: key_version_in_both_lists
cases.description: Key version 1 of authority J is active and also archived, and the head is dated after the archived record's end. The list gives that version no one window: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_version_twice_in_one_list
cases.description: Key version 2 of authority J is held twice among the active versions: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_reused_under_a_later_version
cases.description: Authority L holds one key under version 1, archived, and under version 9, active. A head dated past the archive end under 9 would reopen the retired key: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_version_with_two_keys
cases.description: Authority M holds version 1 twice, with a different key in each record, so the list does not say which key version 1 is: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_list_effective_from_lower_case
cases.description: Authority B's key version 1 takes effect in lower case t and z, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to be inside the key's window: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_list_effective_from_offset_plus_zero
cases.description: Authority B's key version 1 takes effect with the offset +00:00, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to be inside the key's window: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_list_effective_from_second_60
cases.description: Authority B's key version 1 takes effect at second 60, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to be inside the key's window: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_retired_in_unpadded_base64
cases.description: Authority B also holds its key retired under version 8, without padding. The record would read as a second key, so the retirement would not count: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_retired_in_hex
cases.description: The same record in hex, which decodes as base64 to 48 bytes: (f) fails on the length.

cases.name: key_retired_with_trailing_bits
cases.description: The same record in standard base64 with a trailing bit set: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_retired_as_spki
cases.description: The same record as an SPKI text, which is 16 characters and then the key's own standard text, so a reader searching the list finds the key: 44 bytes, (f) fails.

cases.name: key_retired_after_a_zero_byte
cases.description: The same record with a zero byte before the key: 33 bytes, (f) fails.

cases.name: key_retired_one_byte_short
cases.description: The same record with the key's last byte cut: 31 bytes, (f) fails.

cases.name: key_retired_empty
cases.description: A record of B with an empty key: (f) fails.

cases.name: ml_dsa_65_record_with_an_ed25519_key
cases.description: Authority B holds its 32-byte key under the label ML-DSA-65, whose keys are 1952 bytes: (f) fails on the length.

cases.name: ml_dsa_65_key_in_unpadded_base64
cases.description: Authority B holds an ML-DSA-65 key without its padding: (f) fails.

cases.name: ml_dsa_65_key_in_hex
cases.description: Authority B holds an ML-DSA-65 key in hex, which decodes as base64 to 2928 bytes: (f) fails on the length.

cases.name: ml_dsa_65_key_as_spki
cases.description: Authority B holds an ML-DSA-65 key as the base64 of its SPKI, 1974 bytes: (f) fails on the length.

cases.name: ml_dsa_65_key_after_a_zero_byte
cases.description: Authority B holds an ML-DSA-65 key with a zero byte before it, 1953 bytes: (f) fails on the length.

cases.name: ml_dsa_65_key_one_byte_short
cases.description: Authority B holds an ML-DSA-65 key with its last byte cut, 1951 bytes: (f) fails on the length.

cases.name: key_under_another_authority_in_unpadded_base64
cases.description: Authority D lists B's key without padding, which would hide that two authorities hold it: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_under_another_authority_in_hex
cases.description: Authority D lists B's key in hex: (f) fails on the length.

cases.name: key_under_another_authority_as_spki_under_eddsa
cases.description: Authority D lists B's key as SPKI under the label EdDSA. The label is read first, so (f) fails on it.

cases.name: key_retired_under_a_lower_case_label
cases.description: Authority B also holds its key retired under version 8, labelled in lower case. Only Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 are known labels: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_retired_under_the_label_eddsa
cases.description: Authority B also holds its key retired under version 8, labelled EdDSA, the JOSE name for Ed25519. Only Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 are known labels: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_retired_under_a_label_with_a_trailing_space
cases.description: Authority B also holds its key retired under version 8, labelled with a trailing space. Only Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 are known labels: (f) fails.

cases.name: key_retired_under_an_empty_label
cases.description: Authority B also holds its key retired under version 8, labelled empty. Only Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 are known labels: (f) fails.

cases.name: record_under_an_unknown_algorithm
cases.description: Authority B holds an ML-DSA-87 record with a key of that algorithm's length. ML-DSA-87 is not a known label: (f) fails.

cases.name: fingerprint_of_another_key
cases.description: Authority B holds another key under version 8, with B's own fingerprint, so the list would show B's fingerprint retired: (f) fails.

cases.name: fingerprint_under_another_authority
cases.description: Authority D holds another key with B's fingerprint, so the list would show B's fingerprint under D: (f) fails.

cases.name: ml_dsa_65_record_with_another_keys_fingerprint
cases.description: Authority B holds an ML-DSA-65 record of that algorithm's length with B's Ed25519 fingerprint. The fingerprint is read under every label: (f) fails.

cases.name: fingerprint_in_upper_case_hex
cases.description: Authority B holds its key with the fingerprint in upper-case hex: (f) fails.

cases.name: version_with_a_leading_zero
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version "01", which is not the decimal text of an integer: (f) fails.

cases.name: version_with_a_plus_sign
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version "+1", which is not the decimal text of an integer: (f) fails.

cases.name: version_with_a_leading_space
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version " 1", which is not the decimal text of an integer: (f) fails.

cases.name: version_with_an_underscore
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version "1_0", which is not the decimal text of an integer: (f) fails.

cases.name: version_as_a_decimal_fraction
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version "1.0", which is not the decimal text of an integer: (f) fails.

cases.name: version_with_a_letter
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version "v8", which is not the decimal text of an integer: (f) fails.

cases.name: version_minus_zero
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version "-0", which is not the decimal text of an integer: (f) fails.

cases.name: version_past_the_largest_integer
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version "9223372036854775808", which is not the decimal text of an integer: (f) fails.

cases.name: version_zero
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version "0". Versions run from 1: the registry writes none lower, and a document whose version cannot be read is under version 0 to its signature. (f) fails.

cases.name: version_minus_one
cases.description: Authority B holds another key archived under version "-1". Versions run from 1: the registry writes none lower, and a document whose version cannot be read is under version 0 to its signature. (f) fails.

cases.name: ml_dsa_65_record_under_a_leading_zero_version
cases.description: Authority B holds an ML-DSA-65 key of that length under version "01": the version is read under every label, so (f) fails.

cases.name: key_under_two_spellings_of_a_version
cases.description: Authority K holds one key under version 1, archived, and under 01, active. A signature reads 01 as 1, so the list would give the retired key a second window: (f) fails.

cases.name: record_of_another_algorithm_and_length
cases.description: Authority B also holds an ML-DSA-65 record with a key of that algorithm's length, 1952 bytes, in standard base64. The record is inside the grammar and names another key, so nothing fails.

cases.name: key_retired_under_no_label
cases.description: Authority B also holds its key retired under version 8 with no label, which reads as Ed25519. The record is read, so B holds its key twice: (f) fails.

cases.name: largest_version
cases.description: Authority B holds another key under version 9223372036854775807, the largest signed 64-bit integer: inside the grammar, so nothing fails.

cases.name: refused_record_among_the_active_versions
cases.description: Authority B holds an active record without padding: active records are read too, so (f) fails.

cases.name: two_refused_records_under_two_authorities
cases.description: Authority B holds a refused record under version 8 and authority D one under version 7. Authorities are read in byte order of authority_id, so (f) names B's.

cases.name: two_refused_records_under_one_authority
cases.description: Authority B holds a refused archived record under version 8 and a refused active one under version 9. Active records are read before archived ones, so (f) names 9.

cases.name: two_refused_records_in_one_list
cases.description: Authority B holds two refused archived records, version 9 before version 8. Each list is read in its order, not by version, so (f) names 9.

cases.name: authority_id_with_a_cyrillic_letter
cases.description: The list adds an authority whose id is B's with the e of example written as the Cyrillic letter U+0435, holding version 1 with another key, archived before the head. It would read as B's version 1 retired beside B's own. A list authority id has the head alphabet, read before its records: (f) fails.

cases.name: authority_id_with_a_zero_width_space
cases.description: The list adds an authority whose id is B's followed by a zero-width space, holding version 1 with another key, archived before the head. It would read as B's version 1 retired beside B's own. A list authority id has the head alphabet, read before its records: (f) fails.

cases.name: authority_id_with_a_trailing_space
cases.description: The list adds an authority whose id is B's followed by a space, holding version 1 with another key, archived before the head. It would read as B's version 1 retired beside B's own. A list authority id has the head alphabet, read before its records: (f) fails.

cases.name: authority_id_in_upper_case
cases.description: The list adds an authority whose id is B's in upper case, holding version 1 with another key, archived before the head. It would read as B's version 1 retired beside B's own. A list authority id has the head alphabet, read before its records: (f) fails.

cases.name: authority_id_empty
cases.description: The list adds an authority whose id is B's emptied, holding version 1 with another key, archived before the head. It would read as B's version 1 retired beside B's own. A list authority id has the head alphabet, read before its records: (f) fails.

cases.name: authority_id_of_129_bytes
cases.description: The list adds an authority whose id is B's lengthened to 129 bytes, holding version 1 with another key, archived before the head. It would read as B's version 1 retired beside B's own. A list authority id has the head alphabet, read before its records: (f) fails.

cases.name: authority_id_in_upper_case_with_no_records
cases.description: The list adds a revoked authority whose id is B's in upper case and which holds no record. It would show a revoked authority that reads as B. Its id is read although it holds no key: (f) fails.

cases.name: authority_id_of_128_bytes_with_a_dot_and_an_underscore
cases.description: The list adds an authority whose id is 128 bytes long and holds a dot and an underscore, holding version 1 with a key no other authority lists. The id is inside the alphabet, so nothing fails.

cases.name: refused_record_at_its_fingerprint_before_its_version
cases.description: Authority B holds a record whose fingerprint and version are both outside the grammar. The fingerprint is read first, so (f) names it.

cases.name: refused_record_beside_a_head_under_an_unlisted_authority
cases.description: A head under an authority the key list does not carry, which alone fails with head_signing_key_unknown, under a list holding a refused record: the refusal comes first.

cases.name: refused_record_with_no_heads
cases.description: No heads, under a list holding a refused record: (f) still fails, and the proof is listed as having no handed head.

cases.name: refused_record_with_a_malformed_head
cases.description: A malformed head, under a list holding a refused record: (a) fails on the head and (f) on the list.

cases.name: refused_record_gives_no_signer_reason
cases.description: A local-signer proof and a hosted proof with no heads, under a list in which authority D holds the local signer's key in hex. A refused list says nothing a reason could rest on, so both are listed as having no handed head, not as local_signer and unmarked_authority.

cases.name: head_issued_before_proof
cases.description: The head was issued a second before the proof it names ended: (c) fails.

cases.name: head_issued_in_the_second_the_proof_ended
cases.description: The proof ended at 00:06:00.750 and the head was issued at 00:06:00. Times are compared to the second, so nothing fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_unreadable
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at cannot be read as a time, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_milliseconds
cases.description: The named proof ended at 2026-10-28T00:30:00.123Z, a fraction of three digits, as the emitter writes it. The time grammar reads it, and the head is issued after it, so nothing fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_nanoseconds
cases.description: The named proof ended at 2026-10-28T00:31:00.123456789Z, a fraction of nine digits. The time grammar reads it, and the head is issued after it, so nothing fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_second_60
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at '2026-10-28T00:32:60Z' has second 60, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_lower_case_t
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at '2026-10-28t00:33:00Z' has a lower case t, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_lower_case_z
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at '2026-10-28T00:34:00z' has a lower case z, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_space_separator
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at '2026-10-28 00:35:00Z' has a space in place of T, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_offset_plus_zero
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at '2026-10-28T00:36:00+00:00' has the offset +00:00 in place of Z, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_offset_minus_zero
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at '2026-10-28T00:37:00-00:00' has the offset -00:00, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_offset_plus_14
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at '2026-10-28T14:38:00+14:00' has the offset +14:00, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_year_0000
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at '0000-10-28T00:39:00Z' has year 0000, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: proof_end_time_fraction_13_digits
cases.description: The named proof's destroyed_at '2026-10-28T00:40:00.1234567890123Z' has a fraction of thirteen digits, which the time grammar does not read, so the head is not shown to come after it: (c) fails.

cases.name: malformed_type_of_a_later_version
cases.description: A later head type, which this verifier does not know. (a) fails with head_malformed at head.type; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_proof_sequence_zero
cases.description: proof_sequence 0: sequences start at 1. (a) fails with head_malformed at head.proof_sequence; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_proof_sequence_float
cases.description: proof_sequence 1.0: a JSON number with a fraction part is not an integer. (a) fails with head_malformed at the head as a whole; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_proof_sequence_string
cases.description: proof_sequence "1": a string is not an integer. (a) fails with head_malformed at the head as a whole; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_proof_sequence_2_pow_53
cases.description: proof_sequence 2^53: above 2^53 - 1, the largest integer RFC 8785 writes exactly. (a) fails with head_malformed at head.proof_sequence; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_proof_sequence_negative
cases.description: proof_sequence -1: not a non-negative integer. (a) fails with head_malformed at the head as a whole; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_unknown_field_in_head
cases.description: An extra field inside the signed head body. (a) fails with head_malformed at the head as a whole; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_unknown_field_beside_head
cases.description: An extra top-level field beside the head, outside the signed bytes. (a) fails with head_malformed at the head as a whole; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_authority_id_empty
cases.description: authority_id "": an authority has a name. (a) fails with head_malformed at head.authority_id; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_authority_id_uppercase
cases.description: authority_id with an upper case letter: its characters are a-z, 0-9, ., _ and -. (a) fails with head_malformed at head.authority_id; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_authority_id_129_bytes
cases.description: authority_id of 129 bytes: at most 128. (a) fails with head_malformed at head.authority_id; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_authority_id_non_ascii
cases.description: authority_id with a non-ASCII character. (a) fails with head_malformed at head.authority_id; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_authority_id_missing
cases.description: A head with no authority_id. (a) fails with head_malformed at the head as a whole; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_authority_id_beside_head
cases.description: authority_id beside the head, outside the signed bytes. (a) fails with head_malformed at the head as a whole; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_signature_without_base64_prefix
cases.description: The signature without its base64: prefix. (a) fails with head_malformed at signature; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_issued_at_second_60
cases.description: issued_at 2026-10-28T23:59:60Z: seconds run from 00 to 59 on every date. (a) fails with head_malformed at head.issued_at; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_signing_key_version_empty
cases.description: An empty signing_key_version: a key version has a name. (a) fails with head_malformed at signing_key_version; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.

cases.name: malformed_signing_key_version_writes_a_line
cases.description: A signing_key_version holding a newline, a forged check line and a terminal erase sequence: it has the alphabet of authority_id. (a) fails with head_malformed at signing_key_version; (b), (c) and (f) are not checked, and proof 1 is unwitnessed.
